title: data/resolution.json
description: How the actor registry merged names across sources. The Methodology page publishes it.

ambiguities.description: Aliases that name two or more ATT&CK groups, so no merge was made.

unresolved_names.description: Report actor tags that resolved to no actor, most frequent first, at most 200.

source_record_count.description: Actor records read from every source, evidence-only sources included.

actor_count.description: Actors after merging, including any not published because only evidence-only sources know them.

merge_count.description: Source records folded into another record's actor: source_record_count minus actor_count.

evidence_edge_count.description: Shared-alias edges that joined two records. One merge can rest on several edges.

non_actor_name_count.description: Names typed as malware or a tool rather than an actor.

paperMatch.description: The registry measured against the paper's actor names. The build computes this, not the registry.

names_total.description: Distinct actor names in the paper's report data (Zenodo 16869733).

resolved.description: Of those, names the registry resolves to one actor.

typed_non_actor.description: Of those, names the registry types as malware or a tool.

match_rate.description: resolved / names_total, or null when the paper's data is unavailable.

alias.description: The normalized alias key, as names.norm() returns it.

candidates.description: The ATT&CK groups the alias names, sorted.

typed_as.description: malware or tool when the registry typed the name as software, else null.

actorId.description: An ATT&CK group ID such as G0007, or a lower-case ASCII slug for an actor ATT&CK does not track. The ID is also the actor's file name and URL segment, so it has no colons, slashes or spaces, and it is never 'index'.

label.description: Non-empty text with no leading or trailing whitespace and no line breaks.
